item.title: Hamamatsu Kite Festival: Giant Kite Battles Over the Dunes — Guide
item.description: The Hamamatsu Festival, held every year over Golden Week (3–5 May), is famous for its giant kite battles, in which more than a hundred neighbourhood teams fly enormous kites — some several metres across, each painted with their district’s emblem — above the Nakatajima sand dunes, deliberately crossing lines to cut rivals from the sky amid trumpet fanfares and chanting. The tradition began as a celebration of firstborn children and continues today, with evenings bringing a second spectacle as ornately carved palace-like floats parade through the city streets.

item.title: Naha Hari Guide: Okinawa's Dragon Boat Race & Dates
item.description: The Naha Hari (Haarii) is one of Okinawa’s great seasonal spectacles — a colourful dragon boat festival held at Naha Port over Golden Week (May 3–5). Crews paddle ornate dragon-prowed boats called haarii-bune in thunderous races that pray for maritime safety and a good catch, a tradition with centuries-old roots and Chinese ties. With races, food stalls, music and fireworks, it’s a lively, family-friendly festival and a great reason to be in Naha in early May.
